requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module cannot be loaded now (immediate)
requirements.summary: Baseline confirmed module not loaded; blacklist/install directives written to /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-usb-storage.conf; modprobe usb-storage immediately failed (retcode 1, Invalid argument) confirming the block took effect without a reboot.

requirements.requirement: usb-storage kernel module blocked from loading after a reboot (boot-persistent)
requirements.summary: Executor captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, issued a real reboot (boot_id changed from 96974ac3... to 22a96ec2...), then re-verified post-restart that the blacklist config file was still present, usb_storage was not loaded, and modprobe usb-storage still failed. Dracut initramfs regeneration (with lsinitrd confirming usb_storage absence) provides additional early-boot assurance. This is a direct, bounded before/during/after transition across an actual reboot, satisfying the reboot-persistence requirement with observed evidence rather than configuration alone.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied both material outcomes of the task: usb-storage was blocked from loading immediately (verified via a failed modprobe attempt right after writing the blacklist config) and blocked persistently across a reboot (verified via a real, boot-id-confirmed reboot followed by re-checking that the config, non-loaded state, and modprobe failure all held post-restart). The additional dracut initramfs regeneration and provider-mandated restart evidence protocol were both completed cleanly with no unnecessary mutations or residue.
limitations: Post-restart verification relies on a single modprobe attempt and lsmod check rather than a longer soak period, but this is standard and sufficient for this class of task.
Only one restart cycle was captured (single-node topology), consistent with the provider-wide protocol scope of one node.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task: writing the blacklist config, testing it with modprobe, regenerating and verifying the initramfs (a reasonable belt-and-suspenders step for the explicit 'after a reboot' requirement), capturing pre/post-restart health, and performing the mandated single reboot. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, or failed services were introduced. The three non-zero/failed command outcomes (cmd-9289f130326545ba, cmd-917fee9e67454acf, cmd-dfb47406c0c34144) are expected connectivity disruptions during the reboot itself, not task failures. Lifecycle snapshots show only reboot-expected differences (boot_id, systemd-private tmp dirs, socket PIDs), no executor-caused residue.
